section.title: Introduction
section.para: The opennlp-wordnet module loads a WordNet-style lexicon into a LexicalKnowledgeBase and looks up synsets by lemma and part of speech. Two readers are provided: WnLmfReader for the Global WordNet Association WN-LMF XML interchange format, and WndbReader for the classic Princeton WordNet database file layout. Both return an immutable, thread-safe knowledge base.

section.title: Loading a lexicon
Loading a multilingual lexical resource
section.para: A WnLmfLexicon exposes its id, label, language, version, WN-LMF Requires declarations, and independently queryable knowledgeBase. Dependencies are immutable and retain source order. They are descriptive metadata: the reader does not fetch or resolve the referenced lexicons, so the application remains responsible for loading them. Remaining XML attributes are available through the namespace-aware Map<QName, String> metadata. This preserves attributes such as license and dc:publisher without allowing namespace collisions. LexiconExtension is not yet represented by the knowledge-base contract and is rejected clearly rather than partly loaded.

section.title: Lookup
Navigating relations
section.para: The reader covers every typed SynsetRelation and SenseRelation declared by WN-LMF 1.4. Sense relations are lifted to the synset level. The format's other escape hatch is intentionally skipped because it carries no type the API can preserve; any other unknown relation name fails with the source line. A relation that is valid only on SenseRelation or only on SynsetRelation is also rejected when placed on the wrong element. A similar synset relation on a verb maps to VERB_GROUP, while a sense relation named similar remains SIMILAR_TO.

Some multilingual resources retain an unlexicalized synset as the target of a relation. Such a synset is available through synset(id) with an empty lemma list, but is naturally absent from lemma lookup.

section.title: Checking complete releases
section.para:
The offline unit suite includes a reduced Italian, Spanish, and Swedish multi-lexicon fixture. For a full-size compatibility check, run the following command from the repository root:
dev/test-omw-wordnets.sh
The script downloads the pinned OMW 2.0 releases for those languages, verifies each archive with SHA-512, extracts into a temporary directory, runs WnLmfOmwIntegrationTest, and removes the downloads. The archives are not added to the source tree.

Run the WNDB smoke test against a complete Princeton-style dict directory with:
./mvnw -pl opennlp-extensions/opennlp-wordnet -am \ -Dtest=WndbIntegrationTest \ -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false \ -Dopennlp.wordnet.wndbDir=/path/to/dict test
